{{short description|American chemist}}
'''Mary Agnes Kaiser''' (June 11, 1948 – July 10, 2011) was an American [[chemist]]. She worked at E. I. DuPont de Nemours and Company, where she was the first woman promoted to senior research fellow.  A woman scientist of distinction,<ref name="Rossiter">{{cite book|last1=Rossiter|first1=Margaret|title=Women Scientists in America; Forging a New World since 1972.|date=2012|publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press|location=Baltimore|isbn=978-1421403632|page=147|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=m_PU_TupLosC&pg=PA147|access-date=1 September 2016}}</ref> she was  internationally known for her work in environmental analytical chemistry.<ref name="Chromatography">{{cite news|title=Mary A. Kaiser|url=http://www.cfdv.org/mary-kaiser|access-date=1 September 2016|work=Chromatography Forum of Delaware Valley|date=2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160325121135/http://cfdv.org/mary-kaiser|archive-date=25 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Kaiser was born in [[Pittston, Pennsylvania]], on June 11, 1948, to Fredolin Kaiser and Agnes Regina Searfoss Kaiser <ref name="Henderson">{{cite book|editor-last1=Henderson|editor-first1=Andrea Kovacs|title=American Men & Women of Science: A Biographical Directory of Today's Leaders in Physical, Biological, and Related Sciences|date=2010|publisher=Gale|location=Detroit|volume=4|chapter=Kaiser, Mary Agnes|edition=28|url=http://go.galegroup.com/ps/i.do?id=GALE%7CCX2469857527&v=2.1&u=othmerloc&it=r&p=GVRL&sw=w&asid=2b8c5619b70577874d78d93c40d0fccb|access-date=1 September 2016}}</ref> and grew up in [[Exeter, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="Newark">{{Cite news|url=http://www.newarkpostonline.com/obituaries/article_99e83613-841b-5dea-95f1-f54ab514c5aa.html|title=Obituaries|date=21 Jul 2011|work=Newark Post|access-date=24 Aug 2016}}</ref> She attended [[Wilkes University|Wilkes College]] and obtained the bachelor's degree in chemistry in 1970.<ref name="Newark" /> She received her master's degree from Saint Joseph's University in 1972, and a PhD in analytical chemistry from [[Villanova University]] in 1976.<ref name="C&EN">{{Cite web|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/89/i42/Mary-Agnes-Kaiser.html?type=paidArticleContent|title=Mary Agnes Kaiser {{!}} Chemical & Engineering News|last=Ainsworth|first=Susan J.|website=cen.acs.org|access-date=2016-08-24}}</ref>  Subsequently, she spent a year as a Graham Perdue Fellow at the [[University of Georgia]], where she worked with Professor Lockhart Burgess (Buck) Rogers.

== Career and research ==
In 1977, Kaiser began working the [[DuPont]] Company, where she was the first woman to be promoted to the level of senior research fellow.<ref name="Newark" />  She worked as a supervisor in the Separations Department DuPont's Central Research and Development Department in Wilmington, Delaware.<ref>{{Citation |title=Edited by |date=1982-01-01 |work=Journal of Chromatography Library |volume=21 |pages=iii |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/chapter/bookseries/pii/S0301477008700939 |access-date=2026-03-16 |publisher=Elsevier |language=en-US}}</ref> Kaiser was an active member of the [[American Chemical Society]], the Chromatography Forum of the Delaware Valley, the [[Eastern Analytical Symposium]], and the [[Federation of Analytical Chemistry and Spectroscopy Societies]].<ref name="Newark" /> In 1985, she was the second woman ever elected chair of the American Chemical Society's Division of Analytical Chemistry, and the first in the modern era.<ref name="Newark" />  She is the only person to have served as the president of the Eastern Analytical Symposium and as chair of the governing board of the Federation of Analytical Chemistry and Spectroscopy Societies.  For her work in environmental chemistry at the DuPont Company, she became internationally known for the analysis of fluorine compounds in the environment.

== Publications ==
Aside from journal articles on various aspects of environmental analytical chemistry, in 1982, Kaiser and Robert L. Grob published ''Environmental Problem Solving Using Gas and Liquid Chromatography''.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Environmental Problem Solving Using Gas and Liquid Chromatography|last=Kaiser|first=Mary|publisher=Elsevier|year=1982|isbn=0-444-42065-7|location=Amsterdam|series=Journal of Chromatography Library, volume 21}}</ref> The book became a best-seller within the field.<ref name="Newark" />

==Personal life==
Kaiser was married to Professor Cecil R. Dybowski on May 12, 1979, at Villanova Chapel at Villanova University. They had a daughter, Marta M. Dybowski, Esquire.  Kaiser died on July 10, 2011, in Newark, Delaware, of the effects of [[metastatic breast cancer]].<ref name="Obituary">{{cite web|title=Mary Agnes Kaiser|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/delawareonline/obituary.aspx?n=mary-agnes-kaiser&pid=152515562|website=The News Journal|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref>

== Awards ==
* 2009, [[American Chemical Society|ACS]] Delaware Section Award for "conspicuous scientific achievement"<ref name="Wang">{{cite journal|last1=Wang|first1=Linda|title=Mary Kaiser Wins Delaware Section Award|journal=Chemical & Engineering News|date=March 23, 2009|volume=87|issue=12|page=50|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/87/i12/Mary-Kaiser-Wins-Delaware-Section.html?type=paidArticleContent|access-date=1 September 2016}}</ref>
* 2004, Award for distinguished service in the advancement of analytical chemistry, ACS Division of Analytical Chemistry<ref name="Division">{{cite web|title=Division Awards Program|url=http://www.analyticalsciences.org/awards.php?action=divisionAward|website=ACS Division of Analytical Chemistry|access-date=1 September 2016}}</ref>
* Villanova University Founders Award<ref name="October">{{cite web|title=October Meeting Notice|url=http://www.cfdv.org/meeting/chromatographic-measurements-fluorine-containing-compounds|website=The Chromatography Forum of Delaware Valley|access-date=1 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090107090101/http://www.cfdv.org/meeting/chromatographic-measurements-fluorine-containing-compounds|archive-date=7 January 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Chromatography Forum of the Delaware Valley Award<ref name="October"/>
